newsitem.title: USA: Ecuador's Concha to present econ plan in Nov - RFTV. [CORRECTED 19:33 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's Concha to present econ plan in Nov - RFTV. [CORRECTED 19:33 GMT]

text.p: Ecuador's Finance Minister Pablo Concha said his country's government will achieve fiscal balance next year through fiscal discipline and improved tax collection.
Concha told Reuters Financial Television 1997 would be a year of severity as Ecuador's economy adjusts. The government will present its economic plan in mid-November, he said.
"The economic plan will bring together two fiscal themes: a tough budgetary discipline and a transformation of Ecuador's tax collection system," Concha said during an interview taped on Wednesday.
Concha said the plan would improve tax collection and include a larger number of taxpayers, meaning the government would not necessarily raise taxes.
The plan would also maintian the modernization of the state and the capitalization of industries.

"I want to achieve fiscal balance in 1997," Concha said. "We want to grow, but we want 1997 to be a year of real growth. It will be a year of severity, a year of adjustments, needed for better development in 1998, 1999 and the future."
Concha said the government hoped to reduce inflation by about 5.0 percentage points next year.
Ecuador will probably end the current year with 25 percent inflation, he said, adding "We are trying to achieve a reduction to 20 percent next year."
Ecuador hopes to return to the international capital markets, Concha also told Reuters.
The minister said Ecuador would seek to issue a international bond by the end of the first quarter of 1997, and expected the issue to be about $200 million and have a maturity of three-to-five years.
Ecuador's meetings with international lending organizations during the IMF/World Bank annual meetings here resulted in further loans to the country, Concha said.
"We have loans approved for more than one billion dollars, whose process of disbursement has been blocked," Concha said. (Corrects status of process of disbursement to blocked)
He said the International Monetary Fund and World Bank would soon be mounting missions to Ecuador.
